determinacy_enumeration: Exactly one reading: the three indexed reads copy element values out of xs (no alias is created, because every alias in Quidra requires a visible '&'), a new independent array value is allocated and bound to 'part' with deep value semantics, xs is not mutated, and each read is bounds-checked with a deterministic abort (exit status 101) on an out-of-range index. Refutation witnesses: an alias reading is not realizable (no '&' is written and grammar.ebnf confines '&' to explicit address contexts); a copy-on-write sharing reading is not materially different because it is unobservable - observed run shows 'part[0] = 99' leaves xs[1] == 20 and a later 'xs[1] = 77' leaves part[0] == 99; a token-substitution reading is not realizable because Quidra has no macro or textual-substitution mechanism (LOW-B-BY-ABSENCE, methodology 03 Rule 1.9.5). [CLASS 1 - `xs` is an integer array (`int[]`): the elements produced are `int` values and `part` is an `int[]`. Witness: the probe file itself prints 20.]

CLASS 2 - `xs` is `bytes`. `xs` is declared OUTSIDE the measured fragment, and Rule 1.1.2 makes its declaration external, so the operand kind is not fixed by the fragment. language.md 'Strings and arithmetic' and numeric-and-bytes.md L75 ('Each element is exactly one byte and has type `uint8`') make the byte-identical fragment produce `uint8` elements and a `uint8[]`. Witness built and run (scratchpad/verify/f11b3.qui): `bytes xs = bytes(5, fill = 20)` with the byte-identical fragment prints 20 as a `uint8`. Materially different from class 1 on Rule 1.2.1 dimension 8 (width and signedness of the value produced) and dimension 6 (element copy width).

CLASS 3 - `xs` is a `string`. language.md L107: indexing a string yields a one-code-point STRING, not a numeric value, so `part` is a `string[]` and the fragment produces a managed text value. Witness built and run (scratchpad/verify/f11s.qui): `string xs = "abcde"` with the byte-identical fragment prints `b`. Materially different from classes 1 and 2 on dimensions 8 (representation), 6 (a managed string value is retained and released where a scalar is not) and 9 (observable result). || CORRECTION: B = 1 previously asserted that every type at the span is written in the region; it is not - `xs` is external, and the operand-kind axis is what produces every peer's B > 1 (Go 3, Zig 6, C++ 4-5, Swift 4). || EXCLUDED CLASSES: (a) a non-copying sub-range/view type - EXCLUDED, LOW-B-BY-ABSENCE, class_id A2-view, missing construct: Quidra has no slice/view type for arrays (`tensor<T>` slices are internal views, but `tensor` is not admissible here because the array-literal form `[a, b, c]` does not produce one), so no completion makes `part` share storage with `xs`; refutation witness: the array literal always constructs a new array value (language.md L109). determinacy_enumeration: Exactly one reading: three nominal class types with deep value semantics are declared, two of them overriding an inherited method under an exactly-matching contract; a monomorphized generic builds a fresh two-element array whose element type is the closed tagged union 'A | B'; element 0 is read under a bounds check that cannot fail here; the match evaluates the subject once and selects an arm from the runtime discriminator over a statically exhaustive closed set; inside the arm the receiver's static type is the narrowed concrete class, so the method that runs is fixed statically. Refutation witnesses for the classes not counted: an A1 'alias' class is not realizable because no '&' is written; an A4 boxed/existential class is not realizable because generics are monomorphized before checking and no boxing form exists (LOW-B-BY-ABSENCE, methodology 03 Rule 1.9.5); an A7 'target may differ between executions' class is not realizable at 'x.tag()' because 'Method selection is static; there is no dynamic dispatch, virtual, or object slicing' (LOW-B-BY-ABSENCE) - the runtime choice happens at the match, not at the call; an A8 'destruction may run user code' class is not realizable because Quidra declares no destructor or finalizer construct (LOW-B-BY-ABSENCE).

hidden_items.why: At the argument sub-sites of `two<A | B>(A(), B())`: an `A` value and a `B` value each acquire a runtime union discriminator as they flow into the `A | B` parameter, with no box, cast, conversion or encode token written at the site. This record's own K06 row states the trigger - "an 'A' value flows into the 'A | B' parameter without a wrapper call; the runtime discriminator is set to 'A'" - and language.md L13 states the rule. The change is observable by the `match` that follows (it selects on the discriminator) and by the layout the value acquires, which satisfies H7's observability test. H7's exclusion is for 'a representation change WRITTEN at the local site (an explicit box/unbox, explicit conversion, explicit encode/decode call)'; a written type ARGUMENT is none of those - Swift was charged H7 for the structurally identical event even though it writes the target type `[Named]` at its site. H3 correctly stays 0: the `match` arm binds `A x` in the same local site as `x.tag()`, so that call has exactly one candidate and the LED gate of s1.2 applies.

complexity_detail.description: 'class' declaration with methods; an implicit receiver supplies member access and there is no source-level 'self'/'this'.
Single inheritance with ':'; multiple inheritance and inheritance cycles are invalid; inherited fields precede the child's own fields in layout.

'override' is required to replace an inherited method and demands an exactly matching result type, parameter names, parameter types and reference authority; 'override' without an inherited target is an error.

Inheritance is member reuse, not implicit subtyping: 'Base value = derived' and 'Base &value = &derived' are invalid, and method selection is static with no dynamic dispatch, virtual or object slicing.
Union type 'T | U' as a runtime tagged union with exactly one active alternative.
Union widening without a wrapper call; the runtime discriminator is adjusted to the destination type.
The type grammar has no parenthesised types: 'type = array_type, { "|", array_type }', so a union element type can only be introduced through a generic type argument.
Generic function declaration with '<T>' and explicit generic call '<...>(...)'.
Monomorphization of each concrete type-argument tuple before checking and lowering; no erasure or boxing.
Generic type arguments may themselves be arrays, unions, or instantiated generic classes; inference applies only when every parameter is uniquely determined.
'T[]' runtime-length array type and the array literal form.
Indexed read 'expr[expr]': int index, zero-based, bounds-checked.
An out-of-range index is a deterministic runtime error with exit status 101.
'match' statement: subject evaluated once; case forms 'T', 'T name', 'none'; case-local binding; automatic narrowing.
Match exhaustiveness is compile-time checked: every alternative exactly once; there is no catch-all arm form.

Converting a class value into a union closes its per-field initialization state: the class must be fully definitely initialized first, so an alternative selected by exhaustive match is known fully initialized.
